result.title: CineAct: Interaction-State Agents for Playable, Branching Film Generation
result.summary: Open video generators such as MiniMax-H3 produce short clips of only several to a dozen seconds per run. To synthesize longer sequences, existing methods either rely on agentic systems following preset scripts, or roll out autoregressively from the previous clip's last frame, losing off-screen states and accumulating hallucinations across turns. Consequently, users still cannot take an explicit goal, choose how to accomplish it, and see that choice persist across subsequent clips. We study goal-grounded interactive video generation, where one goal admits multiple valid approaches, the user's chosen approach must be executed on screen, and its consequences must persist across clips. To this end, we propose CineAct, a state-first agentic framework in which language-model agents handle reasoning while frozen image and video generators serve purely as renderers. Before interaction, the Architect initializes the world as a spatial layout with cameras, an asset library, and a scene graph; at each turn, the system deduces the planned state change, generates a target end frame with an image generator and rigorously verifies it, and synthesizes intermediate motion with an FL2V model. We further introduce a multi-space benchmark covering two suites: long-horizon step execution and open-intent branching admissibility. Experiments show that explicit world-state modeling boosts multi-step rollout consistency over the pixel-only baseline (+11.4 automated, +23.1 human points) and raises paired branching success toward a shared goal by +30.8 points.

AI.brief_summary: CineAct 研究目标驱动的交互式视频生成：语言模型智能体负责推理，冻结的图像与视频生成器仅充当渲染器，通过显式世界状态（空间布局、相机、场景图、资产库）、目标末帧生成与严格验证来保持多片段一致性，并提出多空间基准。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「状态先行」设计、末帧验证与跨片段状态持久化，可能为 LVR 中内部状态是否保留必要信息、以及证据核验与状态更新提供方法线索；但任务是视频生成而非 VLM 推理解题，迁移需核查。
